metadata.title: A job-search agent that shows its evidence
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: I narrate as myself (Nishant), so the persona bookends are dropped: no Liam/Bear greeting, no composer cold open, no verdict card, no Your Turn. Every beat is a drawing, so the hesitant-writer and terms cards are dropped too. The ClaudeTitleOutro (BOUT) is also dropped because its handle is hard-coded to @NikBearBrown; the film closes on a drawn Manim beat, BEND. bookend_check.py's outro check cannot be exempted and will fail by design; art run and art final do not call it.
metadata.audience: INFO 7375 instructor and TAs; hiring managers for data and machine-learning roles
metadata.source_doc: Nishant's verbatim script (2026-11-23); facts in FACTCHECK.md
metadata.author: Nishant U

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Nee-shaant. I'm building a job-search agent for international data and machine-learning graduates.

beats.narration_text: It watches public job boards at e-commerce companies, picks out the new postings that fit one fictional graduate, Priya Nair, and shows the exact line of evidence behind every verdict.

beats.narration_text: This agent does that reading for them, and will say "insufficient" instead of guessing.

beats.narration_text: What's missing is a verdict on each posting that cites the posting itself, and an agent that's honest when it can't tell. That's why mine is worth building.

beats.narration_text: What I need: Python's standard library, my laptop, and my Claude Code login. The judge calls run there, with no API key and no paid compute.

beats.narration_text: How will I know it works? First, against my own labels. I hand-labeled twenty postings, kept ten sealed, and ran the prompt on them once: ten out of ten,

beats.narration_text: Second, with checks that don't trust the agent. In one live run, the loop said "finished, zero new" for an empty board, and an independent check of the raw responses caught it.
